ns2:section.sectionText: FA22 - ENGL 221, Dave Morris Speculative fiction (sf) has enjoyed especially intense popularity over the past decade, and it’s worth asking: what is it about sf that speaks so particularly to our present moment? How does sf help us think in new ways about our most pressing contemporary issues: ecology, identity, justice, equity, and equality? How does sf help us imagine new, better futures as it presents us hope and despair together? In this course, we’ll explore these questions through readings by authors such as Becky Chambers, N.K. Jemisin, Sam J. Miller, Nnedi Okorafor, and Rebecca Roanhorse. Coursework will include active participation in class discussions, weekly responses, and 2-3 analytical essays.
